subject: BYO key transfer orchestration & network guardrails

Date: Fri, 20 Jan 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Initial: BYO key transfer orchestration request

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Acme is preparing a private deployment cutover (VPC + on-prem HSM) and we need to lock down the BYO key transfer orchestration and the network guardrails before we go to production. High-level asks:

- Walkthrough of the transfer process (operator handoff, import vs. wrap, verification).
- Concrete network constraints (ports, outbound egress allowances, mutual TLS endpoints).
- Acceptance criteria for rotation and zeroize rehearsals.
- Any preflight evidence we should prepare for our auditors.

I attached a short requirements doc that includes our current constraints and the vendor list. Would like to schedule a rehearsal week-of Jan 30 if possible.

Attachments: acme_byo_requirements.pdf (summary + vendor list)

Thanks,
Asha Patel
Head of Security Engineering
AcmeCorp
security@acmecorp.com

Date: Fri, 20 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: BYO key transfer orchestration request

Asha —

Appreciate the context and the requirements doc. We've reviewed it and can support the workflow you describe. Quick clarifying questions so we scope the rehearsal correctly:

1) HSM vendor(s): is Acme standardizing on a single appliance (you mention Thales in the doc) or will this be a mixed fleet? That changes the import path.
2) Desired transit: do you want to use a wrapped-key import (Redwood preparing import tokens) or do you plan an encrypted transfer via a customer-side KMIP proxy over Direct Connect?
3) Operator separation: who is the operator that will perform the final unseal/ingest on your side? We'll need a named operator and an emergency contact.
4) Acceptance criteria: do your auditors require signed attestation logs for each step, or are system logs + signed manifest sufficient?

We put together a short checklist and a proposed rehearsal plan (attached). Tentative rehearsal slots: Tue 2028-01-30 10:00PT or Wed 2028-01-31 14:00PT. Which works best for your team?

Attaching: redwood_byo_checklist_v1.pdf

— Hannah Schmitt
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Asha Patel <security@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Jan 2028 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: BYO key transfer orchestration request

Asha / team —

Couple of technical notes from the runtime/ops side that will inform network guardrails and the transfer choreography: 

- Transfer mode: we recommend an "import-token" wrapped flow if Acme's HSM supports it (Thales Luna typically does). That allows us to avoid long-lived remote key unwrapping over the network.
- Split custody: propose a 2-person operator model on the customer side with an operator nonce (OTP) + signed manifest produced by Redwood.
- Rollback & zeroize: rehearsals should include a forced-zeroize scenario. We'll provide an operator runbook that includes an out-of-band attestation step (signed by both operators).
- Network: minimize outbound egress — allow only specific destination IPs (Redwood proxy fleet) on ports 443 and 1024-1040 only for KMIP fallback. All other egress should be blocked. Mutual TLS (mTLS) between your KMIP proxy and our ingestion endpoint is required.
- Monitoring: we will stream audit events to a private S3 (or equivalent) and provide signed manifests back to Acme for every import operation.

I've attached a guardrails matrix with suggested IP ranges, ports, and a short test plan for the rehearsal.

Attachments: network_guardrails_matrix.csv

— Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 23 Jan 2028 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: BYO key transfer orchestration request

Asha —

Following up with the vendor confirmations and an outline for acceptance tests. Per your vendor list, Acme will be using Thales Luna SA 7.6.x. That confirms:

- Supported import flow: wrapped-key import via vendor-provided import tokens (recommended).
- FIPS mode considerations: ensure firmware 7.6.1+ and that your HSM is in FIPS mode before import; we'll validate during preflight.

Acceptance test outline (summary):
- Preflight: network checks (IP allowlist, port reachability), agent health, attestation certificate verification.
- Transfer: perform import with a test key (K1), validate manifest signature, run crypto operations (sign/verify), and then rotate K1 -> K2.
- Zeroize rehearsal: simulate operator compromise and perform controlled zeroize; verify downstream service behavior.

I've uploaded a short vendor CSV and the acceptance test doc to the drive link below; also put a placeholder SOW for your procurement team.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcme-Byo-Playbooks
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/prepare?docId=0B-ACME-SOW-2028

Attachments included for this thread: acme_vendor_summary.csv

— Mina Haddad
